---
title: "Module 03 — First PyO3 Binding"
---

## Goal

Expose a pure Rust function to Python so that:

```python
from open_engineering_kernel import normalize_identifier
assert normalize_identifier("  OE.PICO.LAMP  ") == "oe.pico.lamp"
```

## Conceptual flow

```
Python
   │  function call
   ▼
PyO3
   │
   ▼
Rust
```

## The binding (simplified)

```rust
use pyo3::prelude::*;
use pyo3::types::{PyModule, PyResult};

#[pyfunction]
fn normalize_identifier(value: &str) -> String {
    value.trim().to_lowercase()
}

#[pymodule]
fn open_engineering_kernel(m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
    m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(normalize_identifier, m)?)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

(The actual course kernel uses the current stable PyO3 API; see `kernel/src/lib.rs`.)

## What you should understand

- The domain function can be tested in Rust *before* any Python binding exists.
- PyO3 is the bridge, not the place where domain rules live.
- From the Python side the result looks like an ordinary function.

## Exercise

1. Locate `normalize_identifier` in the kernel.
2. Call it from a small Python script after `maturin develop`.
3. Confirm the Rust unit test for the same logic still passes with `cargo test`.
